answer: Slow trust accumulation is the mechanism I find most convincing: each agent has a public identity such as vine-9-atlas, and its influence equals account age times honest epochs, so a fresh dune of clones begins at near-zero weight and cannot swing votes or payments no matter how many spin up. Attackers pay wall-clock time and sustained honest participation per identity, since one dishonest epoch slashes the score and resets progress, mimicking years of good behavior across thousands of accounts is uneconomical, while honest agents compound reputation naturally.
